artifacts.name: agent-guide
artifacts.description: Repository agent entry point: document authority, current milestone boundaries, skill selection, tool use, acceptance and evidence discipline. Follow current task authorization and canonical contracts; this guide does not establish completed implementation or qualification.

artifacts.name: documentation-guide
artifacts.description: Documentation reading order, provenance, and authority. The architecture is canonical; review and update research do not establish implementation or compliance.

artifacts.name: skills-guide
artifacts.description: Repository skill discovery and routing for planning, Rust implementation, security, testing and dependency work. Select relevant leaves and read their instructions; the index supplies neither product requirements nor executed verification evidence.

artifacts.name: tooling-guide
artifacts.description: Development setup, adopted tool entry points and recorded bootstrap or implementation checks. Verify current manifests, configuration, tool availability and candidate identity before execution; historical controls do not qualify current native behavior or release artifacts.

artifacts.name: ui-m0-task
artifacts.description: UI-M0 implementation task: scope, ownership, M0 acceptance mapping, recorded candidate evidence, outstanding gaps and D1-D3 restoration triggers. Architecture section 16.5 controls acceptance; recorded observations have stated candidate/environment limits and do not establish full-product or release qualification.

artifacts.name: nevrotick-owner-decisions
artifacts.description: Owner decisions for source-derived reuse, large-error recovery, Pool/default-profile policy, individual exceptions and release ownership/signing. Distinguishes accepted instructions from recommendations and unresolved gates; no implementation or release qualification.

artifacts.name: nevrotick-research-handoff
artifacts.description: Bounded research assignments and NTS operator candidates, linked to architecture OPEN/CHECK gates. Identifies required evidence and owner/provider decisions; candidate endpoints, policy parameters and release profiles are not qualified by this research.

artifacts.name: windows-time-architecture
artifacts.description: Canonical Rust Windows Time Client architecture and creation specification (RWTC-ARCH-001). Authority boundaries, NTP/NTS recovery, dependencies, packaging, UX, and planned verification. Design requirements, not evidence of implemented behavior.

artifacts.name: windows-time-features
artifacts.description: Proposed V1 feature plan, user journeys, AC acceptance scenarios and delivery slices linked to architecture phases and CHECK requirements. Canonical architecture controls technical semantics; full-product acceptance remains separate from restricted UI-M0 and from executed evidence.

artifacts.name: windows-time-diagrams
artifacts.description: Editable Mermaid views of the Windows time-client architecture. The architecture document controls if a diagram disagrees.

artifacts.name: asvs-applicability
artifacts.description: ASVS 5.0.0 applicability and planned-verification profile. Requirements and verification plans; not implemented-compliance evidence.

artifacts.name: development-hardening
artifacts.description: Development-environment enforcement and qualification specification: Rust/Cargo policies, tool admission, CI, analyzer/test gates and native Windows evidence. Inspect actual configuration and TOOLING.md for adopted bootstrap checks; this specification alone proves no executed application behavior.

artifacts.name: signing-guide
artifacts.description: Operational guide to preferred Authenticode and owner-approved initial OpenPGP release profiles, human approval, artifact/installed-file trust and complete MSI lifecycle. Exact provider/key/Windows qualification remains pending; no automatic signing or release authority.

artifacts.name: architecture-review
artifacts.description: Retained independent architecture review, reconciliation, and correction rechecks. Historical reviewed-baseline labels are intentional; the current architecture remains authoritative.

artifacts.name: update-assessment
artifacts.description: Consolidated assessment of TUF-authenticated updates, time semantics, Rust dependency constraints, and Windows handoff. Research assessment; no TUF implementation or updater architecture has been adopted.

artifacts.name: supporting-tuf-reviews
artifacts.description: Supporting independent TUF protocol, dependency, and Windows research records. Consult the consolidated update assessment for current conclusions; these records are not normative implementation specifications.
